metadata.title: Reversible vs Irreversible State

props.name: capability
props.remarks: Business capability for classifying system and process state by reversibility to ensure safe resilience outcomes.

props.name: technology-domain
props.remarks: Resilience, recovery, continuity, rollback, degradation, halt, isolation, and decommissioning behaviors.

props.name: architecture-pattern
props.remarks: Foundational Zero Trust pattern defining when system state may be safely reversed, and when it must not be.

props.name: data-pattern
props.remarks: Defines state reversibility classification as trust-relevant data governing resilience decisions.

props.name: nist-guidance
props.remarks: Continuity and recovery controls are constrained by state reversibility classification.

props.name: nist-guidance
props.remarks: Zero Trust guidance requiring explicit authorization for resumption based on context and risk.

metadata.remarks: Reversible vs Irreversible State defines whether system, integration, or device state may be safely restored, resumed, or replayed. This pattern establishes non-equivalence between technical recoverability and safe recovery.

components.title: Reversible State
components.description: State in which restoration or rollback does not invalidate reality or introduce new harm.

implemented-requirements.remarks: Reversible state supports backup restoration without semantic conflict.

components.title: Partially Reversible State
components.description: State in which restoration is technically possible but requires reconciliation or compensation.

implemented-requirements.remarks: Alternate processing may be required to safely continue operations.

components.title: Irreversible State
components.description: State in which restoration, replay, or resume would conceal harm, violate safety, or compound risk.

implemented-requirements.remarks: Recovery must not conflict with safety or mission constraints.

components.title: State Classification Signaling
components.description: Emission of reversibility classification as a resilience eligibility signal.

components.title: State Reversibility Non‑Equivalence Constraints
components.description: Explicitly defines what reversibility does not grant or imply.

implemented-requirements.remarks: Restorability does not imply safety, authorization, or permission to resume.
